description: DynamoDB and Aurora cross-region replication could lead to data inconsistency due to race conditions or network latency issues between regions. This could result in different data versions existing in different regions simultaneously.
A threat actor could gain unauthorized access to the custom merge logic Lambda function, potentially manipulating the conflict resolution process and affecting data integrity across regions.
Attackers could exploit the multi-region architecture to exfiltrate data by targeting the region with potentially weaker security controls or monitoring.
A sophisticated attacker could attempt to intercept and manipulate data during cross-region replication, potentially affecting data integrity and confidentiality.
Misconfiguration or unauthorized changes to AWS Config rules could lead to undetected security issues and compliance violations across regions.
Attackers could attempt to overwhelm the Application Load Balancers in either region, potentially affecting service availability across the entire system.
Inadequate encryption controls for data at rest and in transit could lead to unauthorized access to sensitive information across regions.
Overly permissive or misconfigured IAM roles could lead to unauthorized access to data across regions.
